cases.question: How long does standard shipping take within the same country?

top3.text:
TrackFlow manages last-mile delivery in the United States (Los Angeles) and
Spain (Zaragoza). Delivery commitments vary depending on the service type
contracted by the client brand:

- Standard shipping: 3 to 5 business days within the same country.
- Express shipping: 24 to 48 hours within the same country (available only
  in the Los Angeles metropolitan area and the Zaragoza-Madrid corridor).
- International shipping (between the United States and Spain): 7 to 12
  business days, subject to customs; TrackFlow does not control customs
  hold times.

cases.question: Does TrackFlow guarantee its delivery SLA during Black Friday?

top3.text:
TrackFlow does not guarantee delivery SLA during declared high-demand dates
(Black Friday, Christmas, January Sales in Spain) — during those dates,
delivery times may extend by up to an additional 40%, and this must be
communicated proactively to clients in advance.

cases.question: What compensation applies after two consecutive months below the on-time SLA?

top3.text:
The contractually committed SLA is 90% on-time deliveries per month,
measured by country. If a country falls below 90% for two consecutive
months, the client is entitled to a 5% compensation on that country's
monthly fee, per the standard contract.

cases.question: Are international returns handled by the standard automated process?

top3.text:
International returns (purchased in one country, returned in another) are
not covered by the standard automated process and require manual handling
by Sofía Ramos's team (Returns Manager).

cases.question: Who pays return shipping when TrackFlow delivered the wrong product?

top3.text:
Standard return window: 30 days from delivery, unless the client brand has
configured a different window in their contract.

Return costs: the return shipping cost is covered by the client brand,
unless the reason is a TrackFlow error (product damaged in transit or
wrong delivery), in which case TrackFlow covers it.

cases.question: Which carrier provides reliable international coverage from Los Angeles?
Which carrier has the best coverage in rural areas of Aragón?

top3.text:
Spain (Zaragoza): MRW, SEUR, DHL, and two local last-mile carriers in the
Zaragoza metropolitan area.
- SEUR: best coverage in rural areas of Aragón.
- MRW: most competitive rates for small packages (under 2 kg).
- Local carriers: only available within the Zaragoza metropolitan area, do
  not cover the rest of Spain.

cases.question: Can an account manager manually choose a carrier without approval?

top3.text:
Carrier selection for each shipment is determined by the system based on
destination, weight, product type, and urgency — the account manager does
not manually choose the carrier except for an exception approved by Carlos
Vega (Head of Carrier Operations).

cases.question: When does the long-term inventory fee start and how is it calculated?

top3.text:
- Inventory with more than 180 days of no movement (no sales or outbound)
  pays a "long-term inventory" fee of 150% over the standard rate, starting
  on day 181.

cases.question: Who must approve a preferential storage rate for a high-volume client?

top3.text:
Clients with more than 50 cubic meters of average monthly volume can
negotiate a preferential rate, but that negotiation must always go through
Miguel Torres — an account manager cannot offer storage discounts on their
own.
